(No)minal (D)ropout Rate

Source: R/nod_dropout.R
nod_dropout.Rd

(No)minal (D)ropout Rate

Usage

nod_dropout(
  data.EIR,
  vaccine_init,
  vaccine_end,
  geo_level = "ADM0",
  birth_cohorts = NULL,
  fix_residence = TRUE
)

Arguments

data.EIR

A data frame containing individual vaccination records. See immunABC.EIR for expected structure.

vaccine_init

Initial vaccine to use in nominal dropout calculation.

vaccine_end

Final vaccine to use in nominal dropout calculation.

geo_level

The geographic level to aggregate results by. Must be "ADM0", "ADM1" or "ADM2". If not specified, the default is "ADM0".

birth_cohorts

Birth cohorts to calculate for. As a vector of years.

fix_residence

Logical. This function requires each person to have a single place of residence across all their vaccinations when geo_level is "ADM1" or "ADM2". When a person has more than one residence, TRUE (default) sets all their records to the residence of their most recent vaccination, and FALSE stops with an error.

Value

A data frame with two rows per geographic unit of residence: one for people who received vaccine_init but not vaccine_end (dropout) and one for people who received both (complete). People without vaccine_init are not counted. Columns:

  • ADM1_residence, ADM2_residence: geographic unit of residence (will only appear depending on what is set in geo_level).

  • indicator: A category: either "dropout" or "complete".

  • num: number of people in that category.

  • denom: number of people who received vaccine_init.

  • percent: num / denom * 100.
